messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]
B2: potassium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[K+]]
B3: cesium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[Cs+]]
B4: potassium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[K+]]

ligand:
L1: PPhtBu2 [SMILES CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=CC=C1)C(C)(C)C]
L2: BrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C1=CC(C(C)C)=C(C(C(C)C)=C1)C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L3: X-Phos [SMILES CC(C1=C(C2=CC=CC=C2P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(C(C)C)=CC(C(C)C)=C1)C]
L4: GorlosPhos HBF4 [SMILES CC(OC1=C(P(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3)C(OC(C)C)=CC=C1)C]
L5: tBPh-CPhos [SMILES CN(C)C1=CC=CC(N(C)C)=C1C2=CC=CC=C2P(C(C)(C)C)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L6: PPhMe2 [SMILES CP(C)C1=CC=CC=C1]
L7: PPh2Me [SMILES CP(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2]
L8: CgMe-PPh [SMILES C[C@]1(O2)O[C@](C[C@]2(C)P3C4=CC=CC=C4)(C)O[C@]3(C)C1]
L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L11: P(fur)3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CO1)(C2=CC=CO2)C3=CC=CO3]
L12: PCy3 HBF4 [SMILES P(C1CCCCC1)(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3]

solvent:
S1: N,N-dimethylacetamide [SMILES CC(N(C)C)=O]
S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]
S4: n-butyl acetate [SMILES CCCCOC(C)=O]

concentration:
C1: 0.057 M
C2: 0.1 M
C3: 0.153 M

temperature:
T1: 90 °C
T2: 105 °C
T3: 120 °C

Experiments so far (best first):
B3 | L8 | S3 | C3 | T3 -> 100.0%
B3 | L8 | S3 | C3 | T2 -> 96.4%

Propose exactly 20 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:

picks.reason: Tests whether potassium pivalate can approach the 100% cesium acetate result while retaining the optimized ligand, solvent, concentration, and temperature.
Measures the effect of replacing cesium acetate with cesium pivalate under the otherwise optimized conditions.
Tests potassium acetate under the optimized conditions to complete the comparison of the four bases.
Checks whether the temperature benefit can offset the lower yield previously observed at dilute concentration.
Tests the low-concentration, low-temperature corner to characterize the combined effects of these variables.
Evaluates whether polar DMAc can replace butyronitrile while preserving the strongest base, ligand, and operating conditions.
Tests whether the optimized catalytic system tolerates a nonpolar aromatic solvent.
Evaluates n-butyl acetate as an alternative solvent under the optimized reaction conditions.
Compares the bulky dialkylphosphine L1 with the leading ligand under the best established base, solvent, and operating conditions.
Tests whether BrettPhos can deliver strong activity in the optimized direct arylation environment.
Assesses X-Phos under the optimized conditions to identify a potentially effective alternative biaryl phosphine.
Tests the electron-rich, bulky L4 ligand while holding all other variables at their best observed settings.
Evaluates whether the distinctive tBPh-CPhos scaffold improves activity in the optimized reaction system.
Retests the small phosphine L6 in the leading solvent and base conditions to separate ligand effects from the previously poor setup.
Retests L7 under the optimized conditions because its earlier near-zero yield was obtained with a different base and solvent.
Tests the bulky, electron-rich JackiePhos ligand as an alternative under the best established reaction conditions.
Uses triphenylphosphine as a simpler ligand benchmark against the highly effective L8 system.
Evaluates the distinct tri(furyl)phosphine ligand under the optimized conditions.
Retests PCy3 under the optimized conditions to determine whether its earlier poor result was caused by the previous reaction setup.
Checks whether the leading alternative base performs better at intermediate concentration than it did in the prior lower-temperature comparisons.
